name: lkpi_80211_resume
prose: Precondition: ic->ic_softc is a valid lkpi_hw; the caller does not hold the wiphy lock (taken and released here). The behaviour depends on the global lkpi_suspend_type. Postcondition (linux_80211.c:10097-10160): error starts at 0; it takes and drops the scan lock only to read whether a scan is running and prints a warning if one is (10112-10116). If (lkpi_suspend_type & 0x1) it takes the wiphy lock and calls lkpi_80211_mo_start; a result other than 0 or EEXIST prints a message, unlocks and jumps to err, skipping everything below including the 0x2 step (10121-10128); otherwise it calls lkpi_80211_mo_add_interface for each vif in lhw->lvif_head, stopping with unlock and goto err on the first nonzero result (10130-10141), then unlocks and calls ieee80211_resume_all(ic). The error variable holds the last result, so an EEXIST from mo_start survives to the end only when lhw->lvif_head is empty (any added vif overwrites it with its own result) and the 0x2 step does not run. If (lkpi_suspend_type & 0x2) it takes the wiphy lock, calls lkpi_80211_mo_resume, unlocks, and maps EOPNOTSUPP to 0, overwriting any earlier error (10147-10153). At err it negates a negative error and returns it (10156-10159), so the return value is 0 or a positive errno. The wiphy lock is released on every path in this function.
note: linux_80211.c:10097-10160 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (EEXIST can be returned when the vif list is empty and 0x2 is clear, since error is only overwritten by add_interface/mo_resume); round-15 reviewer RIGHT: an error from mo_start or mo_add_interface goes to err and skips the 0x2 mo_resume (10127, 10139). Old prose's 'suspend-type bit' is the global lkpi_suspend_type.

name: linux_queue_work_on
prose: Precondition: wq and work are valid, work->state holds a WORK_ST_* value (the cpu argument is unused). Postcondition (linux_work.c:131-158): if wq->draining is nonzero it returns !work_pending(work) at once without changing work->state or enqueueing (142-143). Otherwise linux_update_state atomically replaces work->state with states[old] (IDLE, EXEC and CANCEL become WORK_ST_TASK; TIMER stays TIMER; TASK stays TASK, 134-140) and returns the old state, and the function switches on it: for WORK_ST_EXEC or WORK_ST_CANCEL it calls linux_work_exec_unblock(work), which looks up work->work_queue (the queue the work last ran on, not the wq parameter), and if that is non-NULL scans its exec list under WQ_EXEC_LOCK and, if an entry targets this work, clears the target and returns true; in that case queue_work_on returns true without enqueueing (148-149); if the entry is not found (or work_queue is NULL) it falls through to the IDLE case; for WORK_ST_IDLE (and the fall-through) it sets work->work_queue = wq, calls taskqueue_enqueue(wq->taskqueue, &work->work_task) and returns true (151-154); for WORK_ST_TIMER and WORK_ST_TASK (default) it returns false (155-156). The state change to TASK/TIMER has already happened in each non-draining case.
note: linux_work.c:72-82, 93-114, 131-158 read in full. Orig reviewer RIGHT (EXEC/CANCEL with an exec entry found returns true without enqueue, 148-149); round-15 reviewer RIGHT: linux_work_exec_unblock searches work->work_queue (99-104), not the wq parameter.

name: linux_queue_delayed_work_on
prose: Precondition: wq and dwork are valid, delay is a tick count, cpu is a CPU id or WORK_CPU_UNBOUND. Postcondition (linux_work.c:214-268): if wq->draining is nonzero it returns !work_pending(&dwork->work) without further action (226-227). Otherwise delay is clamped to INT_MAX, dwork->timer.mtx is taken, and linux_update_state atomically replaces dwork->work.state with states[old] (IDLE, EXEC and CANCEL become WORK_ST_TIMER; TIMER and TASK unchanged, 217-223); on WORK_ST_TIMER or WORK_ST_TASK the result is false (261-263). On WORK_ST_EXEC or WORK_ST_CANCEL with delay == 0, linux_work_exec_unblock(&dwork->work) (which scans the exec list of dwork->work.work_queue, not of the wq parameter) is called; if it finds and clears an exec entry for this work, the function sets dwork->timer.expires = jiffies and returns true without arming a timer or enqueueing a task (240-243). In the other EXEC/CANCEL cases and for WORK_ST_IDLE it sets dwork->work.work_queue = wq and timer.expires = jiffies + delay, then for delay == 0 enqueues the work task on the queue's taskqueue (linux_delayed_work_enqueue), else arms dwork->timer.callout with callout_reset_on for a cpu other than WORK_CPU_UNBOUND or callout_reset otherwise, and returns true (246-260). The timer mutex is released before returning in all non-draining paths (265-267).
note: linux_work.c:116-123, 214-268 read in full. Both reviewers RIGHT as for linux_queue_work_on: the true-without-arming case for EXEC/CANCEL and the exec list belonging to work_queue (99-104, 240-243).

name: ck_brlock_read_lock
prose: Slice cut the head and shows the tail of ck_brlock_read_trylock; the function described is CK_CC_INLINE static void ck_brlock_read_lock(struct ck_brlock *br, struct ck_brlock_reader *reader) at ck_brlock.h:178-217. Precondition: br is an initialised brlock and reader is the calling thread's reader record (already registered with the lock). Postcondition: returns nothing. If reader->n_readers >= 1 it stores n_readers + 1 and returns (182-185, nested read lock). Otherwise it loops: spin with ck_pr_stall while br->writer is true (188-189); set reader->n_readers to 1 (an atomic fas on x86, a store followed by a store-load fence elsewhere, with an atomic-load or store-load fence after it, 191-207); reload br->writer and break out of the loop if it is false (209-210); if it became true again it stores 0 in reader->n_readers (212) and repeats. After the loop it issues ck_pr_fence_lock() and returns (215-216). This function has no failure return and can spin while a writer holds the lock; it takes no other lock.
note: ck_brlock.h:178-217 read in full. Round-15 reviewer WRONG for this function: the 'return false after steps >= factor' path (262-263) belongs to ck_brlock_read_trylock (219-267), the slice's function; ck_brlock_read_lock has no bound and no return value. Slice cut the head.

It reads and writes only the named memory and takes no locks.
